title: Dedicated capacity reservation & autoscale: roadmap, cycle slices, and OKR mapping
creator: Priya Patel
description: Quarterly roadmap slice that defines how we will align dedicated capacity reservation (commitments) with autoscaling policies and rollout gates. This ticket captures the end-to-end plan for Q2 focused work: (1) a hedging strategy for reservation sizing to reduce overcommit and underprovision risk, (2) a set of autoscale primitives and policy templates for predictable throughput, and (3) measurable OKRs tying SLOs and unit economics to product milestones. The document intentionally maps work into sprint-sized deliveries, articulation of acceptance criteria, decision trade-offs (cost vs latency vs reliability), and dashboards we need to ship before canary rollouts to enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation hedging policy documented and approved by finance and infra: allowed variance bands, refresh cadence
Autoscale policy templates (latency-first, cost-first, hybrid) implemented as RFC and validated in staging with synthetic load
Latency SLOs for dedicated customers: 99th percentile tail under baseline load and under 2x burst load (specific thresholds in SLO doc)
Cost-per-token model updated with reservation amortization and plotted by customer tier
Rollout gating checks built into Console: capacity-reservation health, autoscale events per minute, and fail-open fallback
Dashboard panel (Console) with token-level cost breakdown, reservation utilization, and autoscale events live for internal trials
Runbook for capacity incidents updated with steps referencing new autoscale rollback and commitment unwind procedures

2025-03-21: Autoscale policy RFC merged and engineering implementation plan created

2025-05-30: Post-canary retrospective and success metric sign-off
decisions: Prefer a conservative hedging band (±10%) for Q2 to limit financial exposure; revisit after two quarters of telemetry
Autoscale policies will expose 'cost vs latency' knobs in Console rather than hardcoding in API to keep flexibility for enterprise ops teams
Default reserved commitment term offered will be 6 months (not 12) in Q2 to improve adoption velocity; 12-month pricing to be reintroduced after model validation
risks: Under-hedging could cause frequent capacity shortages during correlated bursts leading to customer outages
Over-hedging increases unit economics and could reduce renewals if price becomes non-competitive
Misaligned metrics between finance and engineering models (amortization window differences) could lead to poor product decisions
Console gating UI complexity could slow canary rollouts if too many false positives are raised by early telemetry
